verdicts.justification: Ran the repro verbatim: crashed with 'File .../hypertools/io/streaming.py, line 264, in _redraw / artist.set_data(full[:, 0], full[:, 1]) / IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 1' -- a bare IndexError at first redraw. The static counterpart hyp.plot(np.sin(np.arange(100)/8)) returns a Figure fine ('static 1-D ok: Figure'), so the expected behavior is fair. Crash on a plausible single-sensor stream, but a narrow input shape: major.

Reproduced independently: streamed iris (stream_init=50, stream_chunk=25) renders a dense straight band of points pinned along the top box edge, while a static plot of the same 150 rows shows two mid-box clusters (my own renders iris_streamed.png / iris_static.png match evidence x5). My own count using the frozen head-box transform from streaming.py (to_box: np.clip(t,-1,1), lines 228-239): 'samples landing outside frozen box (clamped): 100 of 150'. Clamping is described only in code comments; the hyp.plot stream_* docstring (plot.py:979-1004) never mentions it, and no runtime warning fires. Visibly wrong plot on the project's own tutorial dataset: major.
commands_run: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c '<clamp count via stream_info.xform_data, head-box formula from streaming.py>'
